How we choose

Four questions behind every technology choice

  • Will it last?

    We prefer mature, well-supported tools such as .NET, React, Angular, Python and PostgreSQL with long support lifecycles.

  • Can your team run it?

    If you have in-house developers, we build with tools they already know, so you are never locked in to us.

  • What will it cost to host?

    We size cloud services on AWS or Azure to your real traffic and show you the expected monthly cost up front.

  • Is it secure by default?

    Encrypted data, role-based access, regular dependency updates and code review are part of every build.

See these tools at work in our web, mobile, AI and cloud services.

Engineering practices

How we keep code healthy

Good technology choices matter, but so does how the code is written and looked after.

  1. 01

    Code review

    Every change is reviewed by another engineer before it is merged.

  2. 02

    Automated testing

    Tests check critical behaviour so changes don't break what already works.

  3. 03

    CI/CD pipelines

    Builds and deployments are automated, consistent and repeatable.

  4. 04

    Documentation

    Architecture, setup and APIs are documented, so your team can work with the code.

  5. 05

    Dependency updates

    Frameworks and libraries are kept up to date to close known vulnerabilities.

  6. 06

    Monitoring

    Applications are monitored in production so issues are found early.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Can you work with our existing technology stack?

Yes. We work across .NET, Node.js, Python, Java, Angular, React and the major databases and clouds, and we adapt to the tools your team already uses.

Will we be locked in to OneClicq?

No. We use mainstream, well-supported technology and document what we build, so your own team or another partner can maintain it.

Do you use open-source software?

Yes, where it is mature and well supported. We check licences and keep open-source dependencies up to date.

How do you choose between options?

We weigh long-term support, your team's skills, hosting cost and security, and explain the trade-offs before you decide.

Have a technology question?

Whether you are choosing a stack or reviewing an existing system, we're happy to give an honest view.
